card.name: Small words in old travel narratives
card.fires_on: Commas and small linking words (and, to, on, again, been) inside long sentences in old historical or travel accounts. They often fall in an aside such as "with family, goods and stores," just before the main verb.

modes.label: Comma after an aside
modes.description: A comma closing an interruption, right before the main verb of a pioneer or expedition sentence.
modes.example: tied two canoes together and built a platform upon them, and, with family, goods and stores<<,>> towed his primitive craft fifty-five miles

modes.label: Linking word mid-clause
modes.description: A short word such as to, and, on, I or been in the middle of a clause in 19th-century narrative prose.
